lauren: Quick plan: add a tiny "mini-eval" under /optimize that demonstrates a full flow: SDK snippet -> batching + KV/prefix cache effect -> quick quant-profile note. One runnable example people can paste into CI. Who can take the snippet + numbers?

mike: I can do the Python SDK snippet (short, ~20 lines). Will push to branch docs/mini-eval.

anjali: I'll run a small seq-length sweep (e.g. 32 vs 256) on rw-opt-quant-8b in int8 and fp16 and paste a compact before/after table. Will include a token-cost calc.

lauren: Also add a 2-line migration note for legacy batch_* keys pointing to the migration guide.

sam: Found a stale link under /optimize/batching that points to the old quant article. I'll fix and add a redirect note in the PR.

jessica: PR checklist: examples/optimize/mini_eval.py, examples/tests/test_mini_eval.py (smoke + mocks), update nav, short recs block (2 bullets) about cache vs larger batch, mention safe fallback when quant regresses.

mike: Draft snippet (will include comments):
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key="$REDWOOD_KEY")
quant_profile = {"preferred_dtype": "int8"}  # int8 for throughput, fp16 if quality matters
resp = client.generate(
  model="rw-opt-quant-8b",
  input="Summarize in 2 bullets:\n- long user query\n",
  batch_options={"max_batch_latency_ms": 25, "max_batch_size": 6},
  cache={"enable_kv_prefetch": True},
  quant_profile=quant_profile
)
print(resp.text)

anjali: Nice. I'll add numbers like: "seq32 int8: 110ms / 0.045 tokens; seq256 int8: 380ms / 0.18 tokens; seq256 fp16: 430ms / 0.22 tokens" (placeholder until I run).

lauren: Recommendations (2 bullets, non-prescriptive):
- prefer cache for many short repeated prefixes (low latency, high cost savings)
- prefer larger batch when throughput bursts are tolerable and latency budget allows

sam: I'll include the link fix and note the redirect in the PR description.

jessica: Ping @infra to ensure tests are CPU-only (docs CI has no GPUs). Use mocking for model calls.

infra-bot: Reminder: docs CI runs on CPU only. Mark tests accordingly and mock network/model calls.
